title: Fujifilm AI endoscopy at St. Martin De Porres Hospital, Chiayi, marks a 1 to 1.5 cm adenoma in a man in his 50s; pathology shows stage I colorectal cancer, removed endoscopically
summary: After a positive fecal occult blood test, Fujifilm AI endoscopy at St. Martin De Porres Hospital, Chiayi, marked a 1 to 1.5 cm adenoma; pathology: stage I colorectal cancer, removed endoscopically.
account: Three Taiwanese outlets reported on 19 April 2024 on a man in his 50s. He attended free colorectal cancer screening at St. Martin De Porres Hospital in Chiayi City. He tested positive for fecal occult blood and was scheduled for an AI-assisted endoscopy (Liberty Times Net health). Gastroenterologist Zheng Xu-sheng said that the hospital had introduced a Fujifilm 7000-series endoscope in 2023. The hospital installed what it calls the nation's first Fujifilm AI system (Liberty Times Net; Taiwan Good News). During the examination the AI system marked a suspicious polyp with a colored frame and sounded an alert. It was diagnosed as a 1 to 1.5 cm adenoma that biopsy confirmed as stage I colorectal cancer. It was removed immediately through the endoscope (Taiwan Good News; Guan Chuan Media). Zheng said that polyps over 1 cm risk malignant change. He advised free screening every two years after 50 (Guan Chuan Media). The procedure date is not given. Randomized trials of Fujifilm's CAD EYE have produced mixed results. Saitama Medical University authors reported in January 2024 that AI raised adenoma detection. A team in Palencia, Spain, reported in March 2026 that it found no gain among patients referred after a positive stool test, as this man was.
purpose: The Fujifilm AI system is built to mark suspicious polyps on the endoscopic image with a colored frame and sound. The physician then inspects and removes them. Flagging this adenoma was that function.
system: Fujifilm AI endoscopy system on a Fujifilm 7000-series gastrointestinal endoscope (product name not given in the sources)
deployer: St. Martin De Porres Hospital (天主教聖馬爾定醫院), Chiayi

ratings.reason: A stage I colorectal cancer inside a 1 to 1.5 cm adenoma was removed through the endoscope without surgery, according to all three reports. The sources do not demonstrate a survival benefit for this early-stage cancer.

ai_role.statement: The hospital says that the AI system marked the suspicious polyp with a colored frame and a sound during the examination. The physician then diagnosed and removed it. No source says that the physician would have missed a 1 to 1.5 cm polyp in a patient already referred after a positive stool test. Randomized trials of Fujifilm's CAD EYE have produced mixed results: authors of a 2024 Japanese trial found higher adenoma detection with AI, while authors of a 2026 Spanish trial in patients referred after a positive stool test found none. So the AI's share of this detection cannot be separated from the colonoscopy itself.

data.answer:
After a positive fecal occult blood test, Fujifilm AI endoscopy at St. Martin De Porres Hospital, Chiayi, marked a 1 to 1.5 cm adenoma; pathology: stage I colorectal cancer, removed endoscopically.

A positive stool test had already prompted examination, and pathology established cancer. The case does not show that the endoscopist would otherwise have missed the lesion or that more invasive treatment was certainly avoided. Long-term recurrence, survival, and net detection performance are not established by this single report.

data.limitations: A positive stool test had already prompted examination, and pathology established cancer. The case does not show that the endoscopist would otherwise have missed the lesion or that more invasive treatment was certainly avoided. Long-term recurrence, survival, and net detection performance are not established by this single report. Other retained sources, complete methods, and supplementary material were not rechecked in this pass.

display.answer: Three Taiwanese outlets reported the case on 19 April 2024 and quoted the gastroenterologist Zheng Xu-sheng. Liberty Times Net credits its photographs to the hospital. The hospital's own release and the OECD Monitor entry tell the same story. The two randomized trials of CAD EYE, published in January 2024 and March 2026, concern other patients.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: After a positive fecal occult blood test, Fujifilm AI endoscopy at St. Martin De Porres Hospital, Chiayi, marked a 1 to 1.5 cm adenoma; pathology: stage I colorectal cancer, removed endoscopically.
fields.account: Three Taiwanese outlets reported on 19 April 2024 on a man in his 50s. He attended free colorectal cancer screening at St. Martin De Porres Hospital in Chiayi City. He tested positive for fecal occult blood and was scheduled for an AI-assisted endoscopy (Liberty Times Net health). Gastroenterologist Zheng Xu-sheng said that the hospital had introduced a Fujifilm 7000-series endoscope in 2023. The hospital installed what it calls the nation's first Fujifilm AI system (Liberty Times Net; Taiwan Good News). During the examination the AI system marked a suspicious polyp with a colored frame and sounded an alert. It was diagnosed as a 1 to 1.5 cm adenoma that biopsy confirmed as stage I colorectal cancer. It was removed immediately through the endoscope (Taiwan Good News; Guan Chuan Media). Zheng said that polyps over 1 cm risk malignant change. He advised free screening every two years after 50 (Guan Chuan Media). The procedure date is not given. Randomized trials of Fujifilm's CAD EYE have produced mixed results. Saitama Medical University authors reported in January 2024 that AI raised adenoma detection. A team in Palencia, Spain, reported in March 2026 that it found no gain among patients referred after a positive stool test, as this man was.
